title: Industry Funding and Cholesterol Research: A Systematic Review
authors: Barnard ND, Long MB, Ferguson JM, Flores R, Kahleova H
funder: There was no external funding for this project. However, Dr Long, Dr Ferguson, Dr Kahleova, and Mr Flores received compensation from the Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine for their work on this research study.
authorConflicts: Barnard is the uncompensated President of the Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine and the Barnard Medical Center, organizations that promote low-fat, plant-based diets, and receives royalties and honoraria from books, articles and lectures on nutrition; Flores and Kahleova are employees of the Physicians Committee.
result: 211 articles on egg intake and blood cholesterol published to March 2019. Studies were classed industry-funded when supported by egg or poultry industries, companies promoting egg-derived products or industry promotional programmes. The industry-funded share rose from 0 of 9 articles in the 1950s to 25 of 42 (60%) in 2010-2019 (P < .001). Of 153 intervention studies with a determinable effect, net cholesterol increases were reported in 88 of 94 (93%) non-industry-funded and 51 of 59 (86%) industry-funded studies; none reported a significant decrease. Conclusions described net increases as favourable in 29 of 59 (49%) industry-funded and 12 of 94 (13%) non-industry-funded studies. The American Egg Board's research funding is administered by the Egg Nutrition Center. Published online 11 December 2019; issue 2021;15(2):165-172.
